cadenas.propuesta_en: An LLC separates personal and business liability, which matters when you cook over open flame at other people's events. An S corp election can cut self-employment tax once profit is steady; ask your accountant when it pays off.

Apply on your state tax agency website. In many states sales tax applies to the whole catering invoice: the paella, staff and rentals, and in some states the service charge. Confirm your state's rule before you quote.

Bring the Word plan, the Excel projections and written quotes for the van, the paella pans and the burners. SBA 7(a) loans go through participating banks: ask what owner equity they expect and how long approval takes, and do not sign for the van until the loan is approved.
Have an attorney draft your standard paella catering contract

Ask for a 25-50% nonrefundable deposit to hold the date (the pricing calculator suggests 50%), a final payment date, cancellation tiers, a guest minimum, a final guest count date, and service charge versus gratuity. Add a wind, rain and burn ban clause: a canopy over the cooking station, induction with smaller pans indoors (rented, not in the example budget), or paella cooked at the commissary and delivered hot. State that the client buys the wine for the sangria, and add photo permission. Reuse it for every event.

cadenas.propuesta_en: Cooked rice is a TCS food (B. cereus): serve it at 135 °F (57 °C) or higher, or use time as a public health control for 4 hours with a written procedure, a marked start time and discard (Food Code 3-501.19; ask your county if it allows it). FDA Food Code minimums: 165 °F (74 °C) for chicken, 145 °F (63 °C) for 15 seconds for fish and shellfish, 155 °F (68 °C) for 17 seconds for raw Mexican chorizo (Spanish cured chorizo is ready to eat). Never cool leftover paella for reuse: throw it away. Buy seafood only from approved sources and keep shellstock tags for 90 days (3-203.12).
Choose a shared commissary kitchen with room for your sofrito, stock and cleaned seafood: hours, cold and dry storage, space for pans and burners

cadenas.propuesta_en: Visit at least three and ask first: do you allow propane cylinders on site, and where do the pans and burners live? Compare hours, walk-in space and the deposit. A home kitchen is never allowed for catering, and cottage food rules do not cover seafood or cooked rice.
Your health department asks for it with the permit application. It should name your hours, storage areas for pans, burners and cylinders (if allowed) and cleaning duties; keep a signed copy on file.
Apply for the county catering / health permit and ask whether you can cook the rice at the event

Expect an application, a fee, a menu review and an inspection of the commissary and the van. Ask your county directly: can I cook paella on site at a private catered event? Some counties allow it (California calls it limited food preparation, e.g. San Diego County). If not, cook at the commissary and carry the paella hot.

cadenas.es: Obligatorio si se modifica la carrocería
cadenas.propuesta_en: Your catering permit usually does not cover public or community events. Each event may need its own temporary food permit; ask the county health department how far ahead to apply.
Check with your fire marshal on propane, cooking tents and wood-fire setups

cadenas.es: Planos de instalación, flujos y depósitos de agua
cadenas.propuesta_en: Keep the propane station outdoors or under its own cooking canopy, well away from the guest tent. Virginia's fire code, as an example, requires cooking tents at least 20 ft from other tents and LP-gas cylinders outside; your city's rules may differ. Ask about extinguishers and any event or propane permit. Wood-fire cooking only with a permit, and never during a burn ban. Check with your fire marshal.
Buy a used cargo van and have it inspected by a mechanic
Check mileage, service records, payload and tires, and read the title for liens. The van is not refrigerated: plan coolers with ice for raw seafood, and shelving for pans, burners and cylinders.
Title and register the van, and buy commercial auto and inland marine coverage

Register at your state DMV in the business name. Commercial auto covers the van; inland marine covers pans, burners and gear in transit. A cargo van does not need a CDL (that starts at a GVWR of 26,001 lb or more).

Add liquor liability only if your staff serve alcohol the client buys
Skip this unless your staff pour wine the client buys for the sangria; you cannot sell alcohol without a license. Offer a non-alcoholic sangria and ask your broker where you stand.

Open accounts with an approved-source seafood supplier and a cash-and-carry

Buy only from approved sources, such as a seafood distributor, a broadline distributor or Restaurant Depot. Mussels and clams come with the dealer's shellstock tag: keep it for 90 days. Compare delivery minimums and price lists for seafood, chicken and vegetables.

Buy pans in three sizes: 36 in (90 cm), 32 in (80 cm) and 26 in (65 cm), plus 3-ring burners with legs. Light each ring, check the regulator and hoses with soapy water, and run a full cook before your first event. Add eight 20-lb cylinders with regulators and hoses within their date, two extinguishers and a fire blanket, and open an account with a propane refill or exchange service.
Stock hotel pans, sheet pans and utensils
Standardize on hotel pan sizes so everything stacks, travels and fits the carriers. Label pans and lids by dish.

The cooking in front of guests sells the show. Buy long paddles and ladles, wind guards for the burners, a sturdy work table, a cooking canopy, a floor mat and a fire extinguisher you can reach in seconds.

Negotiate a caterer rate and standard delivery and collection times. Rentals are billed to the client, so build them into your proposal.
Choose disposables and packaging for drop-off orders

Use foil pans and lids that survive heat, plus bamboo or plastic plates and flatware for drop-off. Use compostable items where your city requires them, and test that lids do not leak in a moving van. Label each pan with the time it left hot holding and a discard time 4 hours later, or use chafing dishes; ask your county whether it accepts time as a public health control (Food Code 3-501.19).
Set up temperature logging for transport with a data logger
Place a logger in each insulated carrier and in the van's cargo area. Save the report after every event as proof that food stayed at 135 °F (57 °C) or higher.
Run a full test cook for each pan size with your team

cadenas.propuesta_en: Cook with real rice, stock and propane in each pan size, serve a mock buffet and time every step. Note servings per pan and propane used, then use them to calibrate the kit calculator.
Set a staffing plan per event by service style (servers per guest)

A buffet needs roughly one team member per 25 guests. One paella chef can run about three pans at once; add a helper from four pans or 80 guests. Write the ratio down and use it to price labor in every quote.

Train your crew on propane and fire safety: leak checks, extinguishers and shutdown
Teach everyone to check connections with soapy water, where the extinguishers and the fire blanket are, and how to close the cylinder valves. Name who watches the burners at all times during service.

cadenas.propuesta_en: Run a pre-event briefing every time. The nine major US allergens include fish and crustacean shellfish (crab, lobster, shrimp); label mussels and clams too. Watch for egg in the aioli, wheat in the bread and noodle paella, sulfites in frozen shrimp, and cross-contact from shared paddles and pans. Send allergy questions to the paella chef.
Create your brand, logo, 8 paella menu styles and professional photos

Offer seafood, chicken & seafood, chicken & chorizo, Valencian, farm vegetable, paella negra, lobster & seafood and easy-eat peeled seafood. Photograph paella cooked live and the golden socarrat; photos sell catering far better than menus.

3-5 days out, then the day before

Order rice and pantry items with a small buffer, and seafood 1-2 days before with its tags. Prep sofrito, stock and cleaned seafood at the commissary the day before, labeled and chilled, and build one production list with who does what.
